stories.title: Reid Wiseman, the rocketman shooting for the moon in F1 with Mercedes
summary: Yet the newest addition to the paddock is a man whose quietly spoken, understated thoughtfulness and insight is compelling.

Now part of the Mercedes team, Reid Wiseman has been to the moon and with it brings a perspective like no other.Wiseman was one of four astronauts, alongside Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen, who completed the Artemis II lunar flyby in April.

Last month Wiseman, the mission’s commander, became an ambassador for Mercedes’ F1 team, formalising a relationship that had been growing over several years, to the delight of his daughter Katey, a fan of newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli.

stories.title: Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports
summary: The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster and the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer.

It could be a tipping point in the industryThe awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports.

This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but.Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history.

stories.title: ‘When I walked for Burberry I met Kanye West’: the two lives of Bromley footballer Omar Sowunmi
summary: Full-time defender and part-time model, the 31-year-old is happy to shine a light on both sides of his dual career“I was walking down the street one day and someone came up to me and said: ‘I think you should be a model,’” the Bromley defender Omar Sowunmi says.

There are few parallels between the grind of lower-league football and Milan fashion week but the 31-year-old is adept in both worlds.Sowunmi’s dual career mixes trips to Doncaster with visits to Paris.

On Saturday Bromley travel to Reading under their new manager, Karl Robinson, as they attempt to move off the bottom of League One and the centre-back is clear where his focus lies even after his chance encounter with a model agency employee expanded his horizons.

summary: Controversial breaks were financial boon for broadcastersFifa flags possible benefits but says no decision madeFifa’s tender documents for TV rights for the 2030 World Cup includes a provision for broadcasters to sell adverts during hydration breaks in a strong indication the controversial stoppages will be retained.A three-minute break midway through each half was introduced for the first time at all 104 matches at last summer’s World Cup in the interests of player welfare, a radical move that also provided a commercial boon for broadcasters, particularly the rights holders in the United States, Fox Sports and Telemundo.
